messages:
Incident Bot: [ALERT] 8355000000 - PROD streaming: p99 latency spike on /v1/generate-stream (region: us-west-2). Alerting threshold: 1200ms, observed: 3300ms. Affected route: streaming-chat-large. Impact: degraded responses and streaming stalls for ~15% of requests.
Alex P.: ack. I’m oncall. pulling traces.
Maria G.: I see elevated tail latencies in traces: spikes correlate with certain GPU tenancy (node:gpu-7*). p95 up 2x, p99 up ~3x.
Samir R.: checking infra metrics: GPU ECC correctable errors increasing on gpu-7 between 8354999920-8354999990. thermal temp jumped to 93C then throttle.
Kelsey L.: @Alex P. any customer-facing outages?
Alex P.: preliminary: some streaming sessions stalled, many clients got partial chunks then stall. No full 5xx flood. Customer Ops, can you check support queue?
Customer Ops: seeing ~7 tickets mentioning slow streaming and partial responses in same window. Two enterprise customers reported timeouts hitting client-side 10s retry.
ops-rotations: paging oncall rotationed: @Alex P. assigned. If you need handoff, say so.
Alex P.: triage plan: 1) identify nodes with ECC/thermal events 2) drain affected node(s) from serving 3) failover traffic to warm pool/model-variant fallback 4) notify customers. Starting node scan now.
Maria G.: from logs (last 10m):
```
[8354999956] nvidia-smi -q -d ECC
Gpu 7
  ECC Errors
    Volatile: 124 correctable, 3 uncorrectable
    Aggregate: ...
[8354999978] dmesg | grep -i ecc
NVRM: RmInitAdapter failed, ecc error threshold exceeded on GPU 7
thermald: GPU7 temp=93C, throttling engaged
```
Samir R.: confirmed. Node gpu-7 had repeated correctable ECC bursts and then a short uncorrectable event around 8354999980 coinciding with streaming stalls. Host fans reported oscillation.
Alex P.: initiating graceful drain of node gpu-7 from serving pool. Will redirect new sessions away and let in-flight complete with short TTL. Executing drain command: `infractl node drain gpu-7 --reason "thermal/ecc spike"`
Oncall-Bot: Command acknowledged, drain started at 8355000035. Active sessions: 124, will cordon new assign.
Maria G.: also bumping model fallback policy to immediate for streaming-chat-large in us-west-2: route to quantized-medium variant to reduce GPU occupancy. Applying policy now.
Samir R.: applying a minute-level throttle to batch sizes on remaining nodes to keep latency low. `servingctl batch-config set --region us-west-2 --max-batch 8`
Alex P.: live mitigation notes: - drained gpu-7 - applied fallback to quantized-medium for new sessions - reduced batch sizes - increased KV-cache TTL to reduce recompute.
Customer Ops: sending proactive customer note: "We detected transient streaming delays in us-west-2 impacting partial chunk delivery for some sessions. We routed traffic away from affected hardware and applied mitigations; monitoring continues. If you see ongoing issues please reply."
ops-rotations: are we seeing any errors in model runtime (OOM, OOB)?
Maria G.: no OOMs. Memory usage stable on other nodes. CPU load slightly up due to fallback model being less optimized but within headroom.
Samir R.: infrastructure team: need to queue a hardware swap for gpu-7. Likely flaky unit — escalated to hardware-repair. Tagging maintenance ticket INFRA-8432.
Alex P.: status update 8355000120: p95 returned to baseline (~220ms) after reroute/fallback; p99 improving ~700-900ms but still above SLA for a tiny fraction. Streaming stall count down from 15% -> ~1.8%.
Incident Bot: Incident severity auto-evaluated -> SEV2 due to partial customer impact and SLO breach at p99. Recommended: keep oncall, create follow-up postmortem.
Kelsey L.: starting a dedicated incident bridge for deeper logs and hardware chat.
Oncall-Bot: Assigned follow-up owner: Maria G. for post-incident analysis, Samir R. for hardware replacement coordination.
Alex P.: handover: I need to step out in 15m for evening rotation. @Kelsey L. will take primary for live monitoring and customer comms after 8355000180. Handoff notes: mitigations applied, node drained, hardware ticket opened, metrics improving but p99 still not fully healed; recommend 30m watch.
Kelsey L.: I’m taking over. copying remediation steps to incident doc. Quick checklist: confirm drain completed, monitor p99 for 30m, ensure fallback policy rollback path defined, prepare customer update if regressions.
Customer Ops: sending updated note: "Mitigations applied. Performance has improved for most users; we continue monitoring and will update within 1 hour."
Samir R.: hardware team confirmed RMA for gpu-7 delivered to on-site tech, replacement window ETA 4 hours. In the meantime node remains cordoned.
Maria G.: logging artifact snippets for postmortem: aggregate trace ids for affected sessions: trace: [gkY2... , jM9k... , pL2c...] — saved to incident bucket. Also saving `nvidia-smi` snapshots and dmesg extracts.
Alex P.: final note before stepping out: We should add a short-term rule to detect ECC burst patterns and preemptively evacuate nodes when correctable spikes exceed X within Y seconds. Filing infra improvement ticket INFRA-8433.
Kelsey L.: acknowledged. I’ll keep monitoring and will escalate if p99 climbs. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
